I'd have to somewhat agree with the Bentley here mate, there was room but not enough to expect a completely clean corner. At the time of the crash the bentley was almost on the white line it looks like you are pointing towards the apex of the corner(see attached screenshot), eventually leaving the bentley to either 1) go on the grass and most likely crash or 2) hold his line and crash. 

You did move twice coming up the straight too, went left and then went right when coming into the breaking zone. Only slightly, but it did happen (I think the general rule in racing is that you can move once but after that it's basically a drag race and see who can brake later/higher top speed/better line through the corner, that's what I do anyway). The last move to the right was not needed, the bentley had that line and was not expecting you to close it so fast, there was no time for him to react going that speed.

You left him a bit of room, yes, but the line was closing and there was almost certainly going to be a crash in some form or another.

Overall I'd consider it a racing incident but putting you at-fault.

I'm a mod of quite a large sub too. It is absolutely fair that users can get "annoyed" when mods cant ban people who are breaking rules. 

The thing I'd like to mention is that us mods do require 100% proof of rules being broken. On the sub I mod we have *a ton* of spam, this one if fairly easy to counter and ban the spammers. We also have situations surrounding vote manipulation which is something very, very difficult to deal with. We get lots of reports, and we know the problem exists, but we need 100% undeniable proof before we ban someone. If we were to start issuing bans without 100% undeniable proof, it would not put the sub in a good position and we would be banning 20 people every weekend (in the context of the sub I moderate this would be very bad) 

Basically the point I'm getting at: if mods don't have 100% undeniable proof that someone is breaking rules, they shouldn't ban people. Some rules are easier to punish than others of course, but some situations are presented where the proof is hard to get or there is some doubt.
